words.meaning: to outline or foreshadow an idea without giving every detail
words.example: The opening slide adumbrated the strategy that the team would develop in the full presentation.

words.meaning: to examine an idea, assumption, or source closely and critically
words.example: Before approving the forecast, the finance team interrogated the assumptions behind it.

words.meaning: to give greater value, status, or importance to something
words.example: The new promotion criteria valorize collaboration as much as individual performance.

words.meaning: to draw a conclusion that is broader than the available evidence supports
words.example: We should not overgeneralize from one successful pilot to every customer segment.

words.meaning: affecting several groups, areas, or issues at the same time
words.example: Data quality is a crosscutting concern that touches product, finance, and customer support.

phrases.meaning: to finish or arrive just before a deadline
phrases.example: We got the application in under the wire with only ten minutes to spare.

phrases.meaning: to seek easy approval by appealing to simple emotions or popular opinions
phrases.example: The candidate played to the cheap seats instead of explaining how the policy would work.

phrases.term: leave it all on the field
phrases.meaning: to give your maximum effort and hold nothing back
phrases.example: The team left it all on the field during the final client presentation.

phrases.meaning: to be surprised and unprepared when something happens
phrases.example: We were caught flat-footed when the supplier changed its terms without warning.

phrases.meaning: to pressure someone strongly to act, agree, or pay
phrases.example: The landlord put the squeeze on the contractor to finish the repairs before Friday.
